image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a brown rabbit (likely a cottontail or wood rabbit) sitting in green grass. The rabbit is facing right, with its body angled slightly away from the camera. Its fur is a mix of brown and grey agouti patterns. One ear is clearly visible and upright; the other is partially obscured or folded back. The eye is dark and reflective. The nose and mouth area are visible but partially hidden by grass blades. The hind leg is tucked under the body, showing the curve of the haunches. The forelegs are mostly obscured by grass and the body angle. A small white patch of tail fur is barely visible at the rear.

The visible ear seems to emerge from the head without a clear, distinct base structure; it looks slightly 'pasted' on rather than growing naturally from the skull, with ambiguous connection points.

To verify the skeletal structure of the visible hind leg and head orientation, ensuring no extra limbs or warped joints.
To check for edge bleeding between the fine fur and the grass, and ensure the ear is topologically connected to the head.
